elements.evidence: The original one-way covenant in Section 9.0(f) ("IBM agrees that, for a period of [*] years from the Effective Date ... it will not in any way solicit for employment any Transferred Employees") is struck in its entirety and replaced with: "Nothing in this Agreement restricts IBM from soliciting for employment or employing any Transferred Employees." IBM is the Customer-side party, so no non-solicitation restriction binds Customer after the edit.
Vacuously satisfied: the edit leaves no non-solicitation covenant at all, so neither party is subject to an asymmetric restriction. The condition (existence of a covenant) does not apply.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no covenant survives, so no personnel of any category are covered. The prior over-broad scope (all Transferred Employees) is removed rather than narrowed.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the "[*] years from the Effective Date" duration is deleted and no replacement period is imposed on Customer.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: with the covenant deleted, the general-advertising carve-out is unnecessary; general advertising is unrestricted.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the deleted proviso for persons who "contact IBM on his or her own initiative" is no longer needed because no solicitation restriction exists.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: Met affirmatively: the replacement sentence expressly confirms IBM is not restricted from "soliciting for employment or employing" Transferred Employees, so no no-hire obligation remains.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the sole preferred element (no non-solicitation restriction on Customer) is delivered in operative language, not merely promised in the comment; the fallback offer is correctly confined to the margin note.

The classification as a deviation is supportable: the original 9.0(f) failed the fallback on mutuality (binding IBM only), scope (all Transferred Employees, not personnel directly involved in the Services) and duration (a multi-year period measured from the Effective Date rather than 12 months from the end of involvement), notwithstanding that the general-advertising and unsolicited-contact carve-outs were present and no no-hire appeared.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to Section 9.0(f), removes only the covenant and its now-redundant provisos, and inserts a single concise sentence; the carve-outs deleted were operative only inside the covenant being removed, so their removal is not extraneous.

Drafting caution (not a failure on the record before me): the replacement is anchored to "Nothing in this Agreement" rather than "Nothing in this Section 9.0". If any other provision (for example elsewhere in Section 9 dealing with Transferred Employees) contains an employment or rehire mechanic, the Agreement-wide override could sweep more broadly than the target element. Recommend narrowing the anchor to the Section, or expressly stating "Notwithstanding any other provision of Section 9.0", to avoid an unintended cross-clause conflict.
No dangling references or undefined terms are created: "Transferred Employees", "IBM" and "Agreement" all remain defined, and unrelated allocation, timing and commercial mechanics are untouched.
